::: {#exm-formal-language}
#### Languages over a and b

Let $\Sigma = \set{\mathtt{a}, \mathtt{b}}$.
Each of these sets is a language (@def-formal-language) over $\Sigma$:

- the empty set $\emptyset$ (@def-empty-set), which has no strings;
- $\set{\lambda}$, which has one string, the empty string;
- $\set{\mathtt{b}, \mathtt{ba}, \mathtt{baa}}$, which has three strings;
- the set of strings with an even number of symbols, which is infinite;
- $\Sigma^*$ itself.

The first two are different languages: $\emptyset$ has no elements, and $\set{\lambda}$ has one.

:::
